Based on the provided documentation, the only vulnerabilities that can be definitively verified as additions to the CISA Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) catalog during the October 1–31, 2026 timeframe are CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619. According to Source [[4]](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.24505719), these two critical, unauthenticated remote code execution flaws, collectively referred to as "PHP2Shell," target the PHP interpreter and were formally added to the KEV catalog five days after their public disclosure in October 2026. 

While Source [[1]](https://www.cisa.gov/known-exploited-vulnerabilities-catalog) was referenced for official catalog data, it returned an empty dataset for the query, which reflects a limitation in the provided snapshot rather than a contradiction of the documented additions. Source [[2]](https://doi.org/10.6084/m9.figshare.34330362) analyzes statistical patterns across CISA advisories from 2020 to October 2026 and links CVEs to the KEV catalog for research purposes, but it does not enumerate specific monthly additions. Similarly, Source [[3]](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23427220) utilizes a KEV catalog snapshot dated October 15, 2026, for IoT replication research but does not provide an itemized list of vulnerabilities added that month. Consequently, constrained to the explicit information available across all provided materials, only the two PHP-related CVEs are verifiable for the specified period. The vendor for both entries is PHP, and the affected product is the PHP interpreter.
